meta.howRead: Every page below was fetched from docs.kalshi.com (or the fee-schedule PDF) with a page-fetch tool on 2026-11-22 and quoted verbatim. Shell curl from this sandbox cannot reach kalshi hosts (TLS reset), which is the limitation earlier sessions reported; the page-fetch tool can, so these pages were read directly rather than cited from memory.
meta.note: A fact here is an official statement. A quote is a short verbatim excerpt, with markdown escapes removed and [..] marking an elision. Nothing in this file is inferred.

facts.claim: The demo Trade API v2 is served at external-api.demo.kalshi.co, with demo-api.kalshi.co also supported.
facts.quote: | Demo | `https://external-api.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/v2` | `https://demo-api.kalshi.co/trade-api/v2` |

facts.claim: The demo WebSocket endpoint is wss://external-api-ws.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/ws/v2, with the demo-api host also supported.
facts.quote: | Demo | `wss://external-api-ws.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/ws/v2` | `wss://demo-api.kalshi.co/trade-api/ws/v2` |

facts.claim: For production, external-api.kalshi.com is recommended and api.elections.kalshi.com is also supported.
facts.quote: | Production | `https://external-api.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2` | `https://api.elections.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2` |

facts.page: API Environments and Endpoints — Request Signing
facts.claim: A signed request covers the full path from the API root and excludes the query string; the host is not signed.
facts.quote: Sign the full request path from the API root, without query parameters. [..] `/trade-api/v2/portfolio/orders` [..] not the hostname and not the query string.

facts.claim: The order book returns bids only, and the ask on one side is the complement of the best bid on the other side.
facts.quote: A **YES BID** at price X is equivalent to a **NO ASK** at price ($1.00 - X)

facts.claim: Levels are ascending by price, so the best bid is the last element of each array.
facts.quote: Arrays are sorted by price in **ascending order** [..] The **highest** bid (best bid) is the **last** element in each array

facts.claim: An empty book and an unknown ticker both return 200 with empty arrays, not 404.
facts.quote: A market with no resting orders returns empty `yes_dollars` and `no_dollars` arrays. So does a ticker that does not match any market: the endpoint returns `200` with empty arrays rather than `404`

facts.claim: The order book is wrapped in orderbook_fp with yes_dollars and no_dollars string pairs [price, count].
facts.quote: The orderbook response is wrapped in an `orderbook_fp` object containing two arrays of bids: `yes_dollars` for YES positions and `no_dollars` for NO positions. Each bid is a two-element string array: `[price_dollars, count_fp]`.

facts.claim: Prices are dollar strings with a _dollars suffix (up to 4 dp) and quantities are _fp strings (2 dp).
facts.quote: **Prices**: fixed-point dollar strings (`_dollars` suffix), up to 4 decimal places [..] **Contract quantities**: fixed-point strings (`_fp` suffix), up to 2 decimal places

facts.claim: REST market status is initialized, active, inactive, closed, determined, disputed, amended or finalized.
facts.quote: | `finalized` | Settlement complete. Positions have been paid out. Terminal state. |

facts.claim: The status filter value settled matches markets whose response status is finalized, and open matches active.
facts.quote: | `settled` | `finalized` |

facts.claim: Timestamp filters are status-specific: min_close_ts pairs with closed, and settled pairs with min_settled_ts.
facts.quote: | min_close_ts, max_close_ts | `closed`, *empty* | [..] | min_settled_ts, max_settled_ts | `settled`, *empty* |

facts.claim: The Market object's required price and size fields are the fixed-point ones: yes_bid_dollars, yes_ask_dollars, volume_fp, open_interest_fp.
facts.quote: - yes_bid_dollars [..] - volume_fp [..] - open_interest_fp

facts.claim: result is yes, no, scalar or empty; a binary market resolves to yes or no.
facts.quote: result: type: string enum: - 'yes' - 'no' - scalar - ''

facts.claim: Candle periods are 1, 60 or 1440 minutes, timestamps are seconds, and one request spans at most 5,000 periods.
facts.quote: Valid values are 1 (1 minute), 60 (1 hour), or 1440 (1 day). [..] One request can span at most 5,000 periods.

facts.claim: A candlestick's trade-price block is OHLC under price, with _dollars fields (close_dollars).
facts.quote: - yes_bid [..] - price: $ref: '#/components/schemas/PriceDistribution' description: >- Open, high, low, close (OHLC) and more data for trade YES contract prices

facts.claim: The general taker fee is round up(M x 0.07 x C x P x (1 - P)).
facts.quote: fees = round up(M x 0.07 x C x P x (1-P)) [..] P = the price of a contract in dollars (50 cents is 0.5) [..] C = the number of contracts being traded [..] M = the multiplier for each contract (default is 1 unless otherwise indicated)

facts.claim: The maker fee is round up(M x 0.0175 x C x P x (1 - P)) with M defaulting to 0, and there is no settlement fee.
facts.quote: fees = round up(M x 0.0175 x C x P x (1-P)) [..] M = the multiplier for each contract (default is 0 unless otherwise indicated) [..] There is no settlement fee.

facts.page: Kalshi Fee Schedule (PDF) — General Trading Fees Table
facts.claim: The summary fee table has four columns: price for 1, fee for 1, price for 100, fee for 100. The one-cent row's fee for 100 is $0.07.
facts.quote: | Price of 1 contract | Fee for 1 contract | Price for 100 contracts | Fee for 100 contracts | [..] | $0.01 | $0.01 | $1.00 | $0.07 |

facts.claim: A fill's trade fee is rounded up to $0.000001, then the balance is aligned to $0.0001 (direct member) or $0.01 (non-direct), with a rebate accumulator.
facts.quote: **Trade fee** | Fee from the fee model, rounded up to the nearest `$0.000001` [..] Direct member balances are aligned to `$0.0001` (`0.01c`) [..] **Net fee** = trade fee + rounding fee - rebate

facts.claim: An event's category field is deprecated; the series-level category is the supported place to read it.
facts.quote: category: type: string description: Event category (deprecated, use series-level category instead).

facts.claim: Markets settled before the historical cutoff are only available through /historical/markets.
facts.quote: Markets that settled before the historical cutoff are only available via `GET /historical/markets`.

facts.page: API Environments and Endpoints — Fill and order updates
facts.claim: The dedicated user WebSocket hosts serve only the fill and user_orders channels; any other channel returns error code 8 there.
facts.quote: These hosts serve the `fill` and `user_orders` channels today [..] Subscribing to any other channel returns error code 8 (`Unknown channel name`), so keep your other subscriptions on the hosts above.
